sources.title: USMLE Content Outline (2026)
sources.notes: Public-release outline. It explicitly highlights geriatric medicine, nutrition, prescription-drug use, veterans and military families, gender-affirming care, and patients with disabilities.

sources.title: Step 1 Exam Content and Specifications
sources.notes: Lists Nutrition at 15-20%, Communication and Interpersonal Skills at 6-9%, and confirms emphasis on graphic, tabular, gross-pathology, microscopic, and specimen interpretation.

sources.title: Enhancements to Nutrition Content on USMLE Step Exams Coming in June 2026
sources.notes: Confirms enhanced nutrition-science content across all three Step exams starting June 2026.

sources.title: Test Delivery Software Updates in Place for Step 1
sources.notes: From May 14, 2026, Step 1 uses fourteen 30-minute blocks, no more than 20 items per block, and includes per-image contrast adjustment. Content, total item count, and total exam length remain unchanged.

sources.title: USMLE Program Conducts Practice Analysis Study
sources.notes: The 2026 practice-analysis study may inform later blueprint updates; it does not establish new current testable content by itself.

sources.title: Proposed Nutrition Competencies for Medical Students and Physician Trainees: A Consensus Statement
sources.notes: USMLE states that the 2026 nutrition enhancement aligns with evidence-based competencies including this consensus statement.

sources.title: What to do in the last 20-30 days before Step 1
sources.notes: Mentions ethics and communication as useful preparation areas. This does not prove exam frequency and must not determine coverage without official support.

sources.title: The Breakdown of USMLE Step 1: What You Need to Know
sources.notes: Secondary educational source; official USMLE materials remain controlling.
